draft.text: You came in because you have been having headaches behind your eyes for a few months.
The headaches are worse in the morning and have gotten more severe over time.
We found that you have a pituitary mass pressing on the optic chiasm.
This is causing vision loss, which is why you have been bumping into door frames.
You also have a low TSH level, but other pituitary hormone levels are normal.
The pituitary mass is significant enough to affect your vision and cause headaches.
You may have a condition called bitemporal hemianopia, which means you are losing vision in the outer parts of each eye.
Visual field testing is scheduled before surgery.
The exact date of the test is not known yet, and the exact size of the pituitary mass from the MRI is also not known.

They have gotten worse over time, from a 3 out of 10 to a 6 out of 10.
They are worse in the morning and last a few hours.
You also mentioned bumping into door frames, which you now know is due to vision loss.
You may have a pituitary mass pressing on the optic chiasm.
